rules.heading: THE RULES EVERY AGENT FOLLOWS ARE ONE FILE, AND A PLAN POINTS AT IT.
rules.quote: `/root/.claude/hub/agent-rules.md` carries the rules every plan used to copy, with a decimal `Rules version: N` line.
rules.says: The rules every agent follows live in one file, /root/.claude/hub/agent-rules.md, which carries a decimal 'Rules version: N' line, and plans point at it instead of copying the rules.

rules.heading: THE RULES EVERY AGENT FOLLOWS ARE ONE FILE, AND A PLAN POINTS AT IT.
rules.quote: A plan that sends agents has a `## Rules` section that is the line `Rules: /root/.claude/hub/agent-rules.md, version N.` or every rule line of the file, whole
rules.says: A plan that sends agents must have a '## Rules' section that is either the line 'Rules: /root/.claude/hub/agent-rules.md, version N.' or every rule line of the file, whole, and the plan is refused otherwise.

rules.heading: THE RULES EVERY AGENT FOLLOWS ARE ONE FILE, AND A PLAN POINTS AT IT.
rules.quote: `rulesGate` sends no step while the version the plan pins is not the file's, without latching.
rules.says: No step is sent while the rules version a plan pins differs from the version in the rules file, and this refusal sets no latch.

rules.heading: THE RULES EVERY AGENT FOLLOWS ARE ONE FILE, AND A PLAN POINTS AT IT.
rules.quote: An agent reads the file by that path, and its first call is that Read, or the Read of the approved plan or of the steps file beside it
rules.says: An agent reads the rules file by its path and makes that Read its first call (or the Read of the approved plan or the steps file beside it, since the plan names the file to an agent sent only a path and step number); every other call of an agent is refused until its own transcript holds an unrefused Read of the rules, except its return, its TaskStop and a progress note or report in the scratchpad.

rules.heading: THE RULES EVERY AGENT FOLLOWS ARE ONE FILE, AND A PLAN POINTS AT IT.
rules.quote: An agent a Workflow starts keeps its transcript below `subagents/workflows/<run>/`, and is found there as well
rules.says: A Workflow-started agent's transcript is kept below subagents/workflows/<run>/ and is found there too (via agentFiles in report.mjs, which the status, the pointer, the stop guard and the fence all read through), and the main thread can read it.

rules.heading: THE RULES EVERY AGENT FOLLOWS ARE ONE FILE, AND A PLAN POINTS AT IT.
rules.quote: The first such refusal sets no latch and says so in its text, and tells the agent to read the rules and go on; a second one latches
rules.says: An agent's first refusal for not having read the rules sets no latch, says so, and tells the agent to read the rules and go on; a second such refusal latches.

rules.heading: THE RULES EVERY AGENT FOLLOWS ARE ONE FILE, AND A PLAN POINTS AT IT.
rules.quote: An agent repairs its own red check once, in a file it wrote in that send, and a second red check ends the step.
rules.says: An agent may repair its own red check once, only in a file it wrote in that send, and a second red check ends the step.

rules.heading: A PLAN'S RULES ARE PART OF WHAT IS APPROVED, SO AN EDIT OF THEM AFTER THE BUTTON NEEDS THE BUTTON AGAIN.
rules.quote: The approved scope is the plan's Goals, Asked, Files and Commands and also its `## Rules` line and its `## Rules of this plan` section.
rules.says: The approved scope of a plan includes its Goals, Asked, Files and Commands and also its '## Rules' line and '## Rules of this plan' section, so rewriting a rule after approval changes what was approved.

rules.heading: A PLAN'S RULES ARE PART OF WHAT IS APPROVED, SO AN EDIT OF THEM AFTER THE BUTTON NEEDS THE BUTTON AGAIN.
rules.quote: `approved-plan-guard.mjs` refuses an edit of either section and names it
rules.says: An edit of the Rules line or the Rules of this plan section after approval is refused and named, and a plan whose rules-version pin has gone stale is approved again at the button and not amended.

rules.heading: A PLAN'S RULES ARE PART OF WHAT IS APPROVED, SO AN EDIT OF THEM AFTER THE BUTTON NEEDS THE BUTTON AGAIN.
rules.quote: the review gate's refusal and the approval block in the status name all six
rules.says: The review gate's refusal and the approval block in the status name all six approved sections (Goals, Asked, Files, Commands, the Rules line and Rules of this plan), not only four.

rules.heading: A PLAN'S RULES ARE PART OF WHAT IS APPROVED, SO AN EDIT OF THEM AFTER THE BUTTON NEEDS THE BUTTON AGAIN.
rules.quote: A marker written before the two joined holds no key for them
rules.says: For an approval marker written before the two rules sections joined the approved scope, the status says the marker does not record them, an edit of either is judged against the plan file as it stands, and the first amendment records both.

rules.heading: A PLAN IS NEVER PUT TO THE BUTTON TWICE, AND A PLAN MODE THE HARNESS BEGAN AT A RESTART IS NOT THE PLAN'S.
rules.quote: A compaction or a resume after the approval can print a plan-mode notice and report the mode as plan though the plan is approved and its step is the next move.
rules.says: After a compaction or resume of an approved plan, a harness-printed plan mode is not the plan's: the approval call is refused saying the plan is approved (with a mark that sets no latch), and every other call is judged as outside plan mode, approved-plan-guard.mjs included.

rules.heading: A PLAN IS NEVER PUT TO THE BUTTON TWICE, AND A PLAN MODE THE HARNESS BEGAN AT A RESTART IS NOT THE PLAN'S.
rules.quote: A plan mode entered after the approval, the `.claude/PLAN-LOCK` marker, a changed plan file, another session's marker, a plan whose every step in Order has a DONE hand-back
rules.says: The restart-plan-mode treatment does not apply, and both guards leave things alone, when plan mode was entered after the approval, a .claude/PLAN-LOCK marker exists, the plan file changed, another session's marker is present, every step in Order has a DONE hand-back, or a caller forced the mode (plan_mode_forced).

rules.heading: A PLAN IS NEVER PUT TO THE BUTTON TWICE, AND A PLAN MODE THE HARNESS BEGAN AT A RESTART IS NOT THE PLAN'S.
rules.quote: and a mode a caller forced (`plan_mode_forced`, which the classifier uses and which must not make every tool a read) leave both halves alone.
rules.says: A plan mode a caller forced (plan_mode_forced, which the classifier uses) is left alone by both guards, and forcing it must not make every tool a read.

rules.heading: A PLAN IS NEVER PUT TO THE BUTTON TWICE, AND A PLAN MODE THE HARNESS BEGAN AT A RESTART IS NOT THE PLAN'S.
rules.quote: An approval given at the button before the gates were installed is recovered at the first call: with no marker, the dispatcher writes it from the transcript's approved `ExitPlanMode` result, once
rules.says: An approval given before the gates were installed is recovered at the first call: with no marker the dispatcher writes one once from the transcript's approved ExitPlanMode result, kept across an edit of the Steps or Order, and written for none of a rejected exit, an edit of an approved section, a later plan mode or a marker already present.

rules.heading: A PLAN IS NEVER PUT TO THE BUTTON TWICE, AND A PLAN MODE THE HARNESS BEGAN AT A RESTART IS NOT THE PLAN'S.
rules.quote: A step end counts only for the plan in force: an agent whose prompt names another plan is not an end of this plan's step with the same number
rules.says: A step end counts only for the plan in force; an agent whose prompt names another plan is not an end of this plan's step of the same number.

rules.heading: THE REPLY GUARD'S RELEASE COMMAND PASSES THE FENCE AND THE LATCH, AND LIFTS THE LATCH ITS OWN REFUSAL SET.
rules.quote: `node /root/.claude/hub/reply-guard.mjs --read <host or call:ID> --said "<words>" --route "<kind>: <how>"`, one plain command, is what a refusal of the reply guard names as the way on.
rules.says: The release command 'node /root/.claude/hub/reply-guard.mjs --read <host or call:ID> --said "<words>" --route "<kind>: <how>"', run as one plain command, is the way on that a reply-guard refusal names, and on the main thread it passes the manager fence and the latch.

rules.heading: THE REPLY GUARD'S RELEASE COMMAND PASSES THE FENCE AND THE LATCH, AND LIFTS THE LATCH ITS OWN REFUSAL SET.
rules.quote: a release of the call the latch was set by lifts that latch; a latch another guard set, an agent's own latch and a release of another call stand.
rules.says: A release of the call that set a reply-guard latch lifts only that latch, while a latch set by another guard, an agent's own latch and a release of a different call stand, and every other gate judges the release command as it judges any command.

rules.heading: THE REPLY GUARD'S RELEASE COMMAND PASSES THE FENCE AND THE LATCH, AND LIFTS THE LATCH ITS OWN REFUSAL SET.
rules.quote: The refusal that names the command says so, and every other gate judges the command as it judges any command.
rules.says: A reply-guard refusal that names the release command must say that it passes the manager fence and the latch, and no other gate gives the command any special treatment.

rules.heading: THE FIRST REPLY UNDER A PLAN, ON THE TOP TIER, NAMES THE TIER AND SAYS WHETHER THE WORK NEEDS IT.
rules.quote: The manager's turns send agents and check results, which need no more than a lesser tier, and a session cannot change its own model
rules.says: The manager's turns need no more than a lesser tier and a session cannot change its own model, so the tier line in the first reply is how a switch gets decided.
rules.live_quote: A session cannot change its own model, and says plainly when the work in front of it does not need the top tier.
rules.missing: That the manager's turns need no more than a lesser tier, and that the first reply under a plan on the top tier carries a tier line naming the tier and whether the work needs it.

rules.heading: THE FIRST REPLY UNDER A PLAN, ON THE TOP TIER, NAMES THE TIER AND SAYS WHETHER THE WORK NEEDS IT.
rules.quote: The status print names the model serving the main thread, read from the `message.model` of the newest main-thread reply
rules.says: The status print names the serving model from the message.model of the newest main-thread reply and never from a key inside a tool's input, and a top-tier id is one carrying 'fable' or 'mythos'.

rules.heading: THE FIRST REPLY UNDER A PLAN, ON THE TOP TIER, NAMES THE TIER AND SAYS WHETHER THE WORK NEEDS IT.
rules.quote: While an approval marker is in force, `stop-guard.mjs` refuses the first reply after the serving model changes to a top-tier id unless its first line names the tier and says whether the work needs it
rules.says: While an approval marker is in force, the first reply after the serving model changes to a top-tier id must have a first line that names the tier and says whether the work needs it, once for each change, or it is refused with the words to use.

rules.heading: AN AGENT MAY BE SENT THE STEPS FILE IN THE PLAN'S PLACE.
rules.quote: Approval, the owner's exit from plan mode in the app and every amendment write `<plan>.steps.md` beside the plan, holding only its Rules, Steps and Commands sections
rules.says: Approval, the owner's exit from plan mode and every amendment write <plan>.steps.md beside the plan, holding only the plan's Rules, Steps and Commands sections.

rules.heading: AN AGENT MAY BE SENT THE STEPS FILE IN THE PLAN'S PLACE.
rules.quote: The dispatch gate accepts a prompt that is the steps file's path and a step number, and refuses it when the file is missing or is not exactly what the plan in force gives
rules.says: An agent may be sent a prompt that is just the steps file's path and a step number, and the dispatch gate refuses it when the file is missing or is not exactly what the plan in force gives, so an agent is never sent a drifted copy.

rules.heading: JUDGEMENT LINES ARE NOT DEMANDED BY ANY GATE.
rules.quote: The gate that demanded them was removed by step 58 of the redesign plan, and the wall line and the review answer its reason; rule 2 of the plans page records it.
rules.says: No gate demands judgement lines any more, because step 58 of the redesign plan removed that gate and the wall line and the review answer its reason.

rules.heading: A PLAN RESTS ON QUOTED EVIDENCE AND ACCOUNTS FOR THE ROADMAP.
rules.quote: A plan that sends agents and whose Files names a repository has a `## What is` section whose bullets each quote, in double quotes, twelve characters or more of a line present in a file the bullet names
rules.says: A plan that sends agents and whose Files names a repository must have a '## What is' section whose bullets each quote, in double quotes, at least twelve characters of a line present in a file the bullet names that a named repository holds.

rules.heading: A PLAN RESTS ON QUOTED EVIDENCE AND ACCOUNTS FOR THE ROADMAP.
rules.quote: a `## Roadmap` section with a bullet for every open item of the repository's `## Next capability release` (the decision number or the title, `in` or `out`, and a reason).
rules.says: Such a plan must also have a '## Roadmap' section with a bullet for every open item of the repository's '## Next capability release', giving the decision number or title, 'in' or 'out', and a reason, or ExitPlanMode is refused.

rules.heading: A PLAN RESTS ON QUOTED EVIDENCE AND ACCOUNTS FOR THE ROADMAP.
rules.quote: A `## Found answered` line may answer a run of findings the plan leaves untouched in one line, `Q-TAG-1 to Q-TAG-12 still queued: <reason>`.
rules.says: A '## Found answered' line may answer a run of findings the plan leaves untouched in a single line of the form 'Q-TAG-1 to Q-TAG-12 still queued: <reason>'.

rules.heading: A PLAN THAT MARKS A ROADMAP ITEM AS WORK HAS READ THE APP'S COMMIT LOG FIRST, AND SAYS WHAT IT SHOWED, ITEM BY ITEM.
rules.quote: `plan-guard.mjs` refuses `ExitPlanMode` for a plan with steps whose `## Roadmap` marks an open item `in`, for a repository whose NOTES.md keeps a roadmap, unless the session's transcript holds, after the plan file was first written, the result of a git log
rules.says: A plan with steps whose Roadmap marks an open item 'in', for a repository whose NOTES.md keeps a roadmap, needs the session transcript to hold, after the plan file was first written, the result of a git log on that repository naming its production and its staging branch, or ExitPlanMode is refused.

rules.heading: A PLAN THAT MARKS A ROADMAP ITEM AS WORK HAS READ THE APP'S COMMIT LOG FIRST, AND SAYS WHAT IT SHOWED, ITEM BY ITEM.
rules.quote: the plan's `## Shipped check` has a line for the item, `NNN: not shipped, read against main and staging on <date>`; a line saying it shipped is refused as work already done
rules.says: The plan's '## Shipped check' section must have a line for each such item reading 'NNN: not shipped, read against main and staging on <date>', and a line saying the item shipped is refused as work already done.

rules.heading: A PLAN THAT MARKS A ROADMAP ITEM AS WORK HAS READ THE APP'S COMMIT LOG FIRST, AND SAYS WHAT IT SHOWED, ITEM BY ITEM.
rules.quote: The manager fence passes that read on the main thread, `git -C <full path>` with log, ls-remote, branch in list mode or show-ref, on a repository of the session or the hub worktree and nothing else of git
rules.says: On the main thread the manager fence passes only the shipped-check read, which is 'git -C <full path>' with log, ls-remote, branch in list mode or show-ref, on a repository of the session or the hub worktree, and nothing else of git.

rules.heading: A PLAN THAT MARKS A ROADMAP ITEM AS WORK HAS READ THE APP'S COMMIT LOG FIRST, AND SAYS WHAT IT SHOWED, ITEM BY ITEM.
rules.quote: (`gitHistoryRead`; `--can` says the same)
rules.says: The --can check reports the same permitted shipped-check git reads as the manager fence does, so the two never disagree about which git reads pass.

rules.heading: A PLAN THAT MARKS A ROADMAP ITEM AS WORK HAS READ THE APP'S COMMIT LOG FIRST, AND SAYS WHAT IT SHOWED, ITEM BY ITEM.
rules.quote: a review agent writes nowhere outside the scratchpad
rules.says: A review agent writes nowhere outside the scratchpad.
rules.live_quote: A file you need for a check is written only in the session's scratchpad. A script there is written before the command that runs it and is run by its full path.

rules.heading: A PLAN THAT MARKS A ROADMAP ITEM AS WORK HAS READ THE APP'S COMMIT LOG FIRST, AND SAYS WHAT IT SHOWED, ITEM BY ITEM.
rules.quote: the stop guard refuses a go-word only where a sentence instructs the owner to give one
rules.says: The stop guard refuses a go-word only where a sentence instructs the owner to give one.

rules.heading: A PLAN THAT MARKS A ROADMAP ITEM AS WORK HAS READ THE APP'S COMMIT LOG FIRST, AND SAYS WHAT IT SHOWED, ITEM BY ITEM.
rules.quote: the review refuses an Order that puts two steps with no shared repository or dependency in sequence
rules.says: The plan review refuses an Order that puts two steps with no shared repository or dependency in sequence.

rules.heading: EACH REPOSITORY'S SETTINGS ALLOW THE COMMAND SHAPES A PLAN LISTS, ONE RULE EACH, AND NOTHING BROADER.
rules.quote: `permissions.allow` in a repository's `.claude/settings.json` holds one prefix rule for each shape the plan's Commands list, never a bare `Bash`, a wildcard alone or a rule for a whole program
rules.says: permissions.allow in a repository's .claude/settings.json holds one prefix rule for each command shape the plan's Commands list, never a bare Bash, a wildcard alone or a rule for a whole program, because in automatic mode the harness itself judges any command no rule names.

rules.heading: EACH REPOSITORY'S SETTINGS ALLOW THE COMMAND SHAPES A PLAN LISTS, ONE RULE EACH, AND NOTHING BROADER.
rules.quote: and the file is parsed after each write because the dispatcher skips a repository whose settings fail to parse.
rules.says: The repository's settings file is parsed after each write, because the dispatcher skips a repository whose settings fail to parse.

rules.heading: EACH REPOSITORY'S SETTINGS ALLOW THE COMMAND SHAPES A PLAN LISTS, ONE RULE EACH, AND NOTHING BROADER.
rules.quote: This holds for a session launched inside that repository; whether it binds a session launched at a parent folder with several repositories under it is not measured.
rules.says: The per-repository settings rule is known to hold for a session launched inside that repository, and whether it binds a session launched at a parent folder with several repositories is not measured.

rules.heading: DOCTRINE PARAGRAPHS ARE REPLACED, NOT ADDED TO, WHEN A GATE ENFORCES THEM WHOLE.
rules.quote: A paragraph a gate enforces whole is replaced by one line, `*Enforced whole by:*` and the gate's file name in backticks
rules.says: A doctrine paragraph that a gate enforces whole is replaced by one line, '*Enforced whole by:*' followed by the gate's file name in backticks, because the doctrine is read in full at every start and its length costs every session, and the test fails when such a line names a file the hub does not have.

rules.heading: DOCTRINE PARAGRAPHS ARE REPLACED, NOT ADDED TO, WHEN A GATE ENFORCES THEM WHOLE.
rules.quote: Which paragraphs those are is the owner's choice.
rules.says: Which doctrine paragraphs count as enforced whole by a gate is the owner's choice.

rules.heading: REPLIES ARE WRITTEN TO THE DOCTRINE'S RULES BEFORE THEY ARE SENT.
rules.quote: The guards are not how a session finds out the format: a guard refusal for a shape the doctrine already names is a defect, not feedback.
rules.says: A session writes each reply to the doctrine's rules before sending it and does not learn the format from the guards, so a guard refusal for a shape the doctrine already names is a defect, not feedback.

rules.heading: A REPLY NEVER NAMES THE OWNER'S FEELING, PROMISES CONDUCT FOR A LATER TURN, OR ASKS FOR A GO-WORD UNDER A CORRECTION.
rules.quote: A REPLY NEVER NAMES THE OWNER'S FEELING
rules.says: A reply never names what the owner feels, because that is not the session's to say.

rules.heading: A REPLY NEVER NAMES THE OWNER'S FEELING, PROMISES CONDUCT FOR A LATER TURN, OR ASKS FOR A GO-WORD UNDER A CORRECTION.
rules.quote: PROMISES CONDUCT FOR A LATER TURN
rules.says: A reply never promises conduct for a later turn, because a promise is only words about a turn the gates hold.

rules.heading: A REPLY NEVER NAMES THE OWNER'S FEELING, PROMISES CONDUCT FOR A LATER TURN, OR ASKS FOR A GO-WORD UNDER A CORRECTION.
rules.quote: OR ASKS FOR A GO-WORD UNDER A CORRECTION
rules.says: A reply whose first line asks for a go-word is refused (once, with the reason) while the owner's newest message is a correction, because a go-word is the owner's to give, and fenced code is set aside in these checks.

rules.heading: A REPLY NEVER NAMES THE OWNER'S FEELING, PROMISES CONDUCT FOR A LATER TURN, OR ASKS FOR A GO-WORD UNDER A CORRECTION.
rules.quote: Say what was wrong and what was done, and stop.
rules.says: When correcting, a reply says what was wrong and what was done and then stops.

rules.heading: THE SUITE RUNS UNDER A PLANTED SESSION, AND ITS PLANTS RUN NARROWED FOR A QUICK LOOK.
rules.quote: `session-guards.test.mjs` replaces the inherited session id with a planted one before any case runs and compares the planted status page and manager notes byte for byte after every case
rules.says: The test suite session-guards.test.mjs replaces the inherited session id with a planted one before any case runs and compares the planted status page and manager notes byte for byte after every case, so a run never rewrites the live session's page.

rules.heading: THE SUITE RUNS UNDER A PLANTED SESSION, AND ITS PLANTS RUN NARROWED FOR A QUICK LOOK.
rules.quote: `--plants --files=a.mjs,b.mjs` or `--plants --touched` runs only the plants of those guard files, `--dry` lists them, and `--case=` narrows the cases
rules.says: For a quick look, '--plants --files=a.mjs,b.mjs' or '--plants --touched' runs only the plants of those guard files, '--dry' lists them and '--case=' narrows the cases, but the full run, once, over the integrated change is the gate.
rules.live_quote: In the hub the suite is the cases and every planted failure, `node session-guards.test.mjs` and then `node session-guards.test.mjs --plants`, and a change to a guard file ... runs both before a push.
rules.missing: The narrowed quick-look switches (--plants --files=..., --plants --touched, --dry, --case=) and that the full run, once, over the integrated change is the gate.

rules.heading: THE SUITE RUNS UNDER A PLANTED SESSION, AND ITS PLANTS RUN NARROWED FOR A QUICK LOOK.
rules.quote: A case returns through the helper that names the failed assertion, never a bare boolean, and one case lists any that does and is not on its declared list.
rules.says: A test case returns through the helper that names the failed assertion and never a bare boolean, and one case lists any case that returns a bare boolean and is not on its declared list.
